# Read Specs

This skill helps an agent locate, read, and summarize the main specification artifacts in a repository so the agent gains a global overview of the project.

## Primary targets
- `PRD.md` — Product Requirements Document: goals, stakeholders, scope, acceptance criteria, milestones.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` or `architecture.md` — Clean architecture overview, layer structure, key design decisions.
- `database-schema.md` (or similarly named files) — Data model details, tables, fields, relations, ER diagrams, constraints, indexes, migrations.
- `technical-stack.md` (or similarly named files) — Languages, frameworks, libraries, infrastructure, CI/CD, runtime environments, third-party services.
- `docs/` folder — Architecture, API specs, deployment guides, runbooks, README files, diagrams, and other supporting docs.

## Purpose
- Find the above files across the repo (top-level and nested) and read their contents.
- Produce a concise global overview describing product intent, data model, and technical choices.
- Extract actionable items, and recommended next reads.

## Search patterns (suggested)
- Glob: `**/PRD.md`
- Glob: `**/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `**/architecture.md` ← NEW
- Glob: `**/database-schema*.md` `**/*schema*.md` `**/data-model*.md`
- Glob: `**/technical-stack*.md` `**/tech-stack*.md` `**/stack.md`
- Folder: `**/docs/**` (read `README.md`, `architecture.md`, `api.md`, `deployment.md`, `runbook.md`, etc.)
- Fallback: look for files named `SPEC.md`, `SPECIFICATION.md`, or `requirements.md`

## Reading order and priorities
1. Top-level `PRD.md` (if present) — extract product goals, scope, stakeholders, acceptance criteria.
2. `technical-stack.md` — understand chosen frameworks, runtimes, infra, and constraints.
3. `database-schema.md` and any `schema` files — capture entities, relationships, key fields, and migrations.
4. `docs/` folder files — pick `architecture.md`, `api.md`, `deployment.md`, `runbook.md`, and READMEs.
5. Any additional spec-like files discovered — read and integrate into the overview.

## What to extract from each file
- PRD: one-paragraph summary, core objectives, target users, success metrics, must-have features, timeline or milestones.
- Database schema: list of core entities/tables, primary keys, foreign keys, major relationships, notable indexes, data retention policies, and diagram references.
- Technical stack: runtime languages, major frameworks, database choices, caching, message queues, hosting/cloud provider, CI/CD, infra tooling.
- Docs folder: architecture decisions, API endpoints and contracts, deployment steps, environment variables, secrets handling, monitoring and runbook items.

## Output format (recommended)
- Overview (2–4 sentences): global one-paragraph summary of product + architecture.
- Files found: ordered list with paths and short description.
- Key extracts per file: bullets of the most important facts.
- Next recommended reads/actions: files or areas to inspect next.

## Heuristics and tips
- Prefer files at repository root first, then `docs/`, then nested directories.
- If `PRD.md` is missing, look for `requirements.md`, `specification.md`, or `README.md` in `docs/`.
- For database information, also scan migration folders (e.g., `migrations/`) for table definitions.
- For technical stack, inspect `*csproj*`, `*sln*`, `*.slnx*`, `Dockerfile`, and infra-as-code files if present.
